reason: The sources provide enough factual data about the Lucy spacecraft's record-breaking asteroid tour, its 12-year trajectory, and its unexpected discoveries to support a surprising 45-second story.
story: NASA's Lucy spacecraft is on a mind-bending twelve-year voyage to explore a record-breaking eight different asteroids. Named after the famous hominin fossil—itself named after the Beatles song 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds'—the spacecraft even carries a disc of lab-grown diamonds on board. Lucy's ultimate destination is the Jupiter Trojan swarms, ancient 'fossils of planet formation' trapped in the giant planet's orbit. To reach them, Lucy uses a complex, looping trajectory with multiple Earth gravity assists. Along the way, it pulled off some incredible surprises. When it flew past the main-belt asteroid Dinkinesh, images revealed not just one, but a tiny satellite that turned out to be a contact binary. Later, during a flyby of another asteroid named Donaldjohanson, Lucy had to navigate autonomously while shielding its instruments from the Sun. As Lucy chases these primordial time capsules, it is reshaping our understanding of the early solar system.
angle: A spacecraft named after a fossil and carrying actual diamonds is on a 12-year cosmic treasure hunt that already discovered hidden moons disguised as contact binaries.

claims.claim: Lucy is a NASA space probe on a twelve-year journey to eight different asteroids.
The Lucy spacecraft is the centerpiece of a US$981 million mission.
The mission is named after the Lucy hominin fossils, which were named after the Beatles song 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds'.
The spacecraft carries a disc made of lab-grown diamonds for its L'TES instrument.
Lucy will visit six Jupiter trojan asteroids and two main belt asteroids.
Jupiter Trojans are asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit, orbiting either ahead of or behind the planet.
Harold F. Levison of the Southwest Research Institute is the principal investigator of the Lucy mission.
Lucy flew by and photographed the asteroid Dinkinesh in November 2023.
During the Dinkinesh flyby, NASA discovered a small satellite orbiting Dinkinesh that was actually a contact binary.
Lucy flew by the main-belt asteroid Donaldjohanson in April 2025.

disputed: Exact total object count estimates for the Trojan swarms vary between thousands and millions; the script should use general terms like swarms or thousands of objects.
